source.title: Open problems on compact constant mean curvature surfaces with boundary

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a compact embedded surface in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by that circle or one of the spherical caps bounded by that circle?
accepted.context_brief: embedded cmc surfaces with circular boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. Is a compact embedded cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a simple closed planar curve in ℝ³, and let Σ be a compact embedded surface of constant mean curvature with boundary C. What hypotheses on the boundary curve C guarantee that Σ lies entirely on one side of the plane containing C? In particular, what can be proved when C is convex?
accepted.context_brief: one-sidedness relative to boundary plane

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Under what conditions on the boundary, a compact embedded cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a planar closed curve C is contained in one side of the boundary plane? and if C is convex?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a compact star-shaped surface in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Is Σ necessarily either the planar disk bounded by the circle or a spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: star-shaped cmc surfaces with circular boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3. Is a compact star-shaped cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a simple closed convex curve contained in a plane P, and let Σ be a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface in ℝ³ with boundary ∂Σ = C. If Σ lies entirely on one side of P, must Σ be a topological disk?
accepted.context_brief: topological type from convex planar boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Let C be a simple closed convex curve in a plane P. Let Σ be a compact embedded cmc surface in ℝ³ with ∂Σ=C. Assuming that Σ lies in one side of P, is Σ a topological disk?

accepted.question_text: Assume the setting of Problem 2.4: C is a simple closed convex curve in a plane P, Σ is a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface with boundary C, and Σ lies on one side of P. If, in addition, Σ is locally a graph over P\D̄ near C, where D is the planar domain bounded by C, must Σ be a bigraph? Equivalently, must there exist a planar domain Ω with D̄ ⊂ Ω̄ such that Σ = Σ₁ ∪ Σ₂, where Σ₁ is a graph over D and Σ₂ is an annulus that is a graph over Ω\D̄?
accepted.context_brief: bigraph structure near convex planar boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Under the same hypothesis of Problem 2.4, if Σ is a graph on P\setminus\overline{D} around C, is Σ a bigraph? that is, is there a planar domain Ω, \overline{D}\subset\overline{Ω}, such that Σ=Σ₁\cupΣ₂, where Σ₁ is a graph on D and Σ₂ is an annulus which it is a graph on Ω\setminus\overline{D}?

accepted.question_text: Let C₁ and C₂ be two convex curves contained in parallel planes. If Σ is a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C₁ ∪ C₂, must Σ be a topological annulus?
accepted.context_brief: two convex boundary components

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6. Let C₁ and C₂ be two convex curves in parallel planes. Is a compact embedded cmc surface spanning C₁∪C₂ a topological annulus?

accepted.question_text: Let C₁ and C₂ be two coaxial circles lying in parallel planes. If Σ is a compact embedded constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C₁ ∪ C₂, must Σ be a surface of revolution?
accepted.context_brief: coaxial circular boundary components

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7. Let C₁ and C₂ be two coaxial circles in parallel planes. Is a compact embedded cmc surface spanning C₁∪C₂ a surface of revolution?

accepted.question_text: If Σ is a topological disk immersed in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle, must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: cmc disks with circular boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8. Is a topological cmc disk spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: If Σ is a stable compact constant-mean-curvature surface spanning a round circle, must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by that circle or a spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: stable cmc surfaces with circular boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9. Is a stable compact cmc surface spanning a circle a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Produce numerical visualizations of the Kapouleas examples of constant-mean-curvature surfaces with circular boundary.
accepted.context_brief: numerical visualization of Kapouleas boundary examples

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10. Give numerical pictures of the Kapouleas’ examples with circular boundary.

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a compact embedded stable surface in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by the circle or a spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: stable embedded circular-boundary case

evidence.quote: Problem 2.11. Is a compact stable embedded cmc surface of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Let Σ be a compact embedded disk in ℝ³ with constant mean curvature and boundary equal to a round circle. Must Σ be either the planar disk bounded by the circle or a spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: embedded cmc disks with circular boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 2.12. Is a compact embedded cmc disk of ℝ³ spanning a circle a planar disk or a spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a simple closed planar curve of length L bounding a planar domain D. For every H in the interval [0, L/(2|D|)], does there exist a constant-mean-curvature H-surface with boundary C? What can be proved in the special cases where C is convex or where C is an ellipse?
accepted.context_brief: existence for prescribed H and planar boundary

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. Let C be a simple planar closed curve. Is there an H-surface bounded by C for each H of the interval [0,L/(2|D|)]? Particularize to the case that C is a convex curve or C is an ellipse.

accepted.question_text: Let C be a simple planar closed curve of length L bounding a planar domain D. Does there exist a constant-mean-curvature H-surface with boundary C when H = L/(2|D|)? If such a surface exists, what geometric properties must it have?
accepted.context_brief: critical mean-curvature existence case

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Let C be a simple planar closed curve. Is there a H-surface bounded by C where H=L/(2|D|)? What can be said about the geometry of this surface?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a closed curve contained in a slab S_w ⊂ ℝ³ of width w, and let H ≠ 0 satisfy |H| < 2/w. Does there exist a topological disk of constant mean curvature H spanning C and entirely contained in the same slab S_w?
accepted.context_brief: cmc disks constrained to a slab

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.3. Let H
ot=0 and let C be a closed curve contained in a slab \mathcal{S}_w\subset\mathbb{R}^{3} of width w such that |H|<2/w. Does an H-topological disk exist spanning C and included in \mathcal{S}_w?

accepted.question_text: Let H ≠ 0 and let Σ be a compact H-surface spanning a circle of radius r, with Σ contained in a slab S_w and |H| < 2/w. Must Σ be a spherical cap? If one strengthens the inequality to the smaller bound asked in the source, must Σ be specifically the small spherical cap?
accepted.context_brief: circular boundary inside a slab

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.4. Let H
ot=0 and let Σ be a compact H-surface spanning a circle \mathbb{S}^{1}(r). If Σ included in the slab \mathcal{S}_w, with |H|<2/w, is Σ a spherical cap? If we replace 2/w by the smaller bound asked there, is Σ a small spherical cap?

accepted.question_text: Is the round sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface contained in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?
accepted.context_brief: closed cmc surfaces in a critical-width slab

evidence.quote: Problem 3.5. Is the sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface included in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a simple planar convex curve contained in a plane P, let D be the planar domain bounded by C, and let Σ be a compact constant-mean-curvature surface spanning C. If Σ is contained in the vertical cylinder D × ℝ, must Σ be a graph over D?
accepted.context_brief: graphicality inside the boundary cylinder

evidence.quote: Problem 3.6. Let C\subset P be a simple planar convex curve. Let Σ be a compact cmc surface spanning C. If Σ is included in D	imes\mathbb{R}, is Σ a graph on D?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a non-circular closed convex planar curve. Does there exist a threshold volume V_C > 0, depending only on C, such that every compact embedded constant-mean-curvature disk Σ spanning C with enclosed volume V satisfies the following trichotomy: (i) if V ≤ V_C, then Σ lies on one side of the boundary plane P; (ii) if V = V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of minimum curvature of C; and (iii) if V > V_C, then Σ has points on both sides of P?
accepted.context_brief: volume threshold for crossing the boundary plane

evidence.quote: Problem 3.7. Let C be a non-circular closed convex planar curve. Prove that there is V_C>0 depending only on C such that, if Σ is a compact cmc embedded disk spanning C and with volume V>0, it holds: (1) If V\leq V_C, then Σ lies in one side of P. (2) If V=V_C, then Σ is tangent to P at the points of minimum curvature of C. (3) If V>V_C, then Σ has points in both sides of P.

accepted.question_text: Let C₁ and C₂ be two simple planar convex curves in ℝ² with disjoint interiors. Does there exist V₀ > 0 such that every constant-mean-curvature surface Σ with boundary C₁ ∪ C₂ and enclosed volume V < V₀ is necessarily disconnected?
accepted.context_brief: small-volume two-boundary-component problem

evidence.quote: Problem 3.8. Let C₁,C₂\subset\mathbb{R}^{2} be two simple planar convex curves with disjoint interiors. Does V₀>0 exist such that if Σ is a cmc surface with boundary C₁\cup C₂ and volume V<V₀, then Σ is not connected.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded convex domain, and consider the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du / sqrt(1 + |Du|²)) = 2H in Ω with boundary condition u = 0 on ∂Ω. Under each of the three assumptions |Ω|H² < π, LH² < 2π, and diam(Ω) < 2/|H|, determine whether this Dirichlet problem is solvable.
accepted.context_brief: Dirichlet problem under weaker convex-domain bounds

evidence.quote: A method to find H-surfaces spanning a given curve is by solving the Dirichlet problem { div Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)=2H in Ω; u=φ in ∂Ω }.
Problem 4.1. Let Ω be a bounded convex domain. Solve the Dirichlet problem (4.1) for φ=0 under each one of the following hypothesis: (1) |Ω|H^2<π. (2) LH^2<2π. (3) diam(Ω)<2/|H|.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded convex domain, and let u solve the constant-mean-curvature Dirichlet problem div(Du / sqrt(1 + |Du|²)) = 2H in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. How can one control the distribution of the convex level curves of u in terms of H? Can Wang’s counterexample on convexity of level sets be extended to the case where Ω is unbounded?
accepted.context_brief: level-set geometry for cmc Dirichlet solutions

evidence.quote: A method to find H-surfaces spanning a given curve is by solving the Dirichlet problem { div Du/sqrt(1+|Du|^2)=2H in Ω; u=φ in ∂Ω }.

Problem 4.2. Suppose that Ω is a bounded convex domain. Let u be a solution (4.1) for φ=0 on ∂Ω. Give a control of the distribution of the convex level curves in terms of the value H. Extend the Wang’s example, if possible, when Ω is not bounded.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded convex domain. Give conditions guaranteeing that a constant-mean-curvature graph over Ω with planar boundary is itself convex.
accepted.context_brief: convexity criteria for cmc graphs

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. Let Ω be a bounded convex domain. Give conditions that assure the convexity of a cmc graph on Ω and with planar boundary.
